title: Introduce preflight credential precheck and stream backpressure hints; coordinate minor cross-SDK parity and version bumps
author: Mariana Ortega
description:
Motivation: We see recurring transient failures in long-lived streaming flows where auth tokens expire or lack a required scope mid-session; consumers then need to handle reconnect logic repeatedly. This PR introduces a lightweight preflight credential precheck in the Python SDK and a set of non-breaking stream backpressure hint attributes to make stream consumers more ergonomic. The changes are designed to be opt-in, minimal impact, and aligned with cross-SDK parity work (parallel small bumps in TypeScript and Go SDKs documented).

Summary of changes: added a preflight check API (Client.check_credentials_preflight) that performs a fast token validation + scope/role probe using the existing auth endpoint; this runs in <200ms on average and can be used by clients before opening streaming sessions. Implemented stream backpressure hints on the StreamHandle object: heuristics fields (preferred_chunk_size, suggested_pause_threshold, suggested_resume_threshold) and two convenience wrappers (stream_generator_with_hints and PauseableStreamAdapter) to make consuming producers/consumers easier. Added telemetry hooks so the console can surface preflight failure rates and mid-stream auth errors (no data leakage; only the error class and timing reported).

Cross-SDK coordination: minor version bumps are proposed for TS and Go SDKs to pick up the matching contract for the preflight probe response and stream hint fields; this PR includes a docs surface file (docs/sdks/cross-sdk-credential-preflight.md) describing the compatibility matrix and migration notes. The Python SDK changes are backwards-compatible: existing callers see no behavioral change unless they opt into the new methods or wrap with the convenience adapters.

Checklist:
- [x] Add preflight API and tests (unit + small integ against staging auth endpoint)
- [x] Add stream hint fields and Python adapters
- [x] Add docs and migration guidance for other SDKs
- [x] Add telemetry counters and expose short-term console dashboard items
- [x] Run full CI and fix lint/test failures

Test plan: unit tests added for preflight validation (including simulated 401/403 and transient network errors), stream adapter tests exercise pause/resume under simulated backpressure, and an integration smoke test was run against staging that exercises preflight then opens a streaming session to ensure no mid-stream auth failures for a 30-minute continuous message stream. CI: all unit + integration checks passed on second run after fixing a flaky mock in test_auth.py.

Risks and mitigations: the preflight probe is best-effort and does not replace server-side authentication checks. The probe includes a short TTL caching layer to avoid excessive auth traffic; TTL defaults to 15s and is configurable. Backpressure hints are advisory only; servers will ignore unknown fields for older deployments. No breaking API changes introduced.

Notes for release: include short 'how to' snippet in 1.28.0 Python changelog and publish cross-SDK migration doc so TS/Go teams can align their minor bumps.

If there are objections to the telemetry fields, we can toggle telemetry behind a feature flag; currently instrumentation is opt-in via client config.
commits: feat(auth): add Client.check_credentials_preflight with TTL cache
feat(stream): add hint fields to StreamHandle and PauseableStreamAdapter wrapper
docs: add cross-sdk credential preflight guide and migration matrix
test(auth): unit + integration tests for preflight error modes
chore(ci): fix flaky test_auth mock and bump pyproject version to 1.28.0-rc
review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice addition. Can the preflight call be optional on Client.__init__? Otherwise we might cause extra latency for simple non-streaming use cases?
Author reply: Yes — preflight is opt-in by default. The client offers run_preflight_on_connect=False and a convenience helper so callers can choose to call it manually.
Sana Patel: Please ensure we don't include any token values in telemetry. Also add a unit test for TTL cache expiry behavior.
Author reply: Agreed. Telemetry only reports error class, HTTP status and duration. Added TTL expiry tests and a doc note about privacy.
Omar Alvarez: small nit: adapter API naming — PauseableStreamAdapter.pause() should be idempotent. Add a comment in adapters.py
Author reply: Fixed. Added idempotency and tests.
release_notes: Python SDK 1.28.0: opt-in preflight credential probe (Client.check_credentials_preflight), advisory stream backpressure hints, PauseableStreamAdapter convenience wrapper, and cross-SDK parity docs. Minor release with no breaking changes.
